title: Codex 0.148.0 gives every input element a per-run id, so no Codex fixture could be recorded
foundBy: session agent, re-recording the Codex fixtures after the host's codex auto-updated

evidence.verified: `make fixtures` records all eight scenarios and passes. `make test-smoke` and `make test-integration` each replay all eight green, 18.1s and 17.7s. TestTheDefaultStripTakesCodexMessageIdsAndLeavesToolCallIds asserts both halves: two runs of one question normalize alike, and two different call_id values still do not.

details:
Codex 0.148.0 attaches an `id` to every element of `input`, minted fresh per run: `msg_01a02023-b134-76d0-b0fe-06cf1a749449` one run and `msg_01a02023-cfca-7a61-9081-2e183aeb3d62` the next.

No rule in the ruleset covered it, so recording a Codex session became impossible. `make fixtures` replays a cassette before it keeps it, and that replay compared a recording against the very run that had produced it and missed on the first request. The failure was not subtle, but it looked like a matching bug rather than a new field.

The field is stripped rather than declared volatile. A volatile path reports every difference it allows, and this one differs on every message of every request, so the session summary would fill with observations about a nonce.

The accompanying test pins the other half of the line. A tool call's `call_id` sits on the exact side of it, and a rule broad enough to take both ids would let a replay agree with a session that called a different tool.
